tools.name: list_recent_drops
tools.description: Recent Pokemon TCG restock alerts across the retailers bujusjujus covers, newest first. Use this to answer "what dropped recently", "has X restocked lately", or to summarise activity for a retailer or time window. Returns a plain array (no cursor) of alerts with id, detectedAt (ISO 8601 UTC), retail

tools.name: search_tracked_products
tools.description: The catalogue of Pokemon TCG products bujusjujus actively tracks, with each one's MSRP. Use this to check whether a product is covered, or to look up the retail price of a set or SKU before judging whether a listing is a fair price. Returns name, retailer and msrp (USD, null when we have no MSRP on

tools.name: get_product_msrp
tools.description: Manufacturer suggested retail price for Pokemon TCG products matching a name. Use this before calling a listing overpriced or a deal good — comparing an asking price to MSRP is the whole judgement. Returns name, retailer and msrp in USD. Products with no MSRP on file are omitted rather than returned

tools.name: get_retailer_stats
tools.description: How many Pokemon TCG drops each retailer had over a window. Use this to answer "who restocks most often" or "which retailer is worth watching". Returns retailer and a drop count, busiest first. Counts include unverified community reports, so treat them as relative activity rather than a precise numb

tools.name: get_in_stock_now
tools.description: Pokemon TCG products that just came in stock, in real time — the same alerts our app subscribers get, at the same moment. Use this when the user wants to buy something NOW or asks "is anything in stock". Returns id, detectedAt, retailer, title, productUrl (the retailer page to buy from), price, msrp

tools.name: wait_for_drop
tools.description: Wait for the next Pokemon TCG restock that matches your filters, and return it the moment it happens (a long-poll: the call stays open up to timeoutSec). Use this to watch for a drop — for example "tell me when a Pitch Black ETB is in stock at MSRP". Call it in a loop: pass back the `cursor` from th

tools.name: set_webhook
tools.description: Register (or replace) the HTTPS endpoint we POST to the instant a matching restock happens — for a server-side AI bot that should not hold a connection open. One webhook per API key; calling again replaces the URL and filters and issues a NEW signing secret. Each POST is JSON { type:"alert", cursor,

tools.name: get_webhook
tools.description: The webhook registered for this API key, if any: url, filters, whether it is active, consecutive failures, the last successful delivery and the last error. Use it to diagnose missing deliveries. Never returns the signing secret.

tools.name: remove_webhook
tools.description: Stop webhook deliveries for this API key and delete its registration, including the signing secret. Use it when the receiving endpoint is being retired. To change the URL or filters, call set_webhook instead.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: set_webhook, get_webhook · Private data: search_tracked_products, get_product_msrp, set_webhook, get_webhook, remove_webhook · Public sink: set_webhook, get_webhook, remove_webhook · Destructive: get_retailer_stats, wait_for_drop, remove_webhook.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: set_webhook, get_webhook · Private data: search_tracked_products, get_product_msrp, set_webhook, get_webhook, remove_webhook · Public sink: set_webhook, get_webhook, remove_webhook · Destructive: get_retailer_stats, wait_for_drop, remove_webhook

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
